builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AttnSR: Attention Step Reward for Long-Horizon Agentic RL
summary: AttnSR replaces outcome-only terminal rewards in long-horizon agentic RL with step-level reward allocations derived from the policy's own attention graph, without a separately trained reward model or extra rollouts. Its costs are modest: attention-graph tracing during training replay, a running baseline for the terminal step, and integration into a PPO-style training loop rather than inference-time overhead. It can fail if policy attention is a poor proxy for step relevance, if rewards reinforce spurious intermediate steps, or if the single-model, two-environment results do not transfer to noisier tools, longer horizons, or different model families.
rationale: It is a low-infrastructure training-time augmentation with a credible quality gain, but the evidence base is narrow and requires validation on the reader's own agent workload before adoption.
technique: Attention-derived step rewards for agentic RL

claims.statement: AttnSR replaces outcome-only terminal rewards in long-horizon agentic RL with step-level reward allocations derived from the policy's own attention graph, without a separately trained reward model or extra rollouts. Its costs are modest: attention-graph tracing during training replay, a running baseline for the terminal step, and integration into a PPO-style training loop rather than inference-time overhead. It can fail if policy attention is a poor proxy for step relevance, if rewards reinforce spurious intermediate steps, or if the single-model, two-environment results do not transfer to noisier tools, longer horizons, or different model families.

On ALFWorld with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, raises final held-out success from 91.2% to 97.1% versus PPO; on ScienceWorld, improves success at every checkpoint while cutting environment interactions by 29.9%.
